ui.note: Upgrade Better Auth and passkey together to 1.7.12. TOTP enrollment explicitly requests totp and checks the response method before reading setup keys or backup codes. Document the response boundary and unchanged explicit native approval. Session startup, transport retry, locale and theme behavior are preserved. Zero 1.11 cached query results retain the prior unknown-result loading and import-activation policies; initializing remains a pending sync state. Document the client database boundary and durable retirement behavior.

release.note: Prepare the first beta, 0.1.0-beta.1 with Android code 13, retain the existing signing certificate and documentation epoch, align release commands, and describe the remaining prerelease and native qualification limits. Generated publication notes now describe a prerelease rather than an alpha.

configuration.note: Align Zero client and cache at 1.11.1 with both upstream Litestream configurations and forks. Preserve app IDs, publications, replication slots and restricted application roles. Document V5 backup defaults, connection budgets and upgrade sequencing.

deployment.note: Rebuild the aligned Zero runtime and optional all-in-one runtime from the same reviewed package and PostgreSQL patch. Retain pinned Node and hardened backup dependencies, add the V5 configuration, and document existing-replica migration, backup and rollback procedures.

native.note: Document desktop cold offline activation from complete unexpired evidence in the OS credential store, exact session binding, fail-closed verification and revocation markers, and native token refresh on socket retry. Existing records need one complete online start; downgrades require signing out stored accounts before installing an older build. Retain queued edits, refuse fallback for trust, HTTP, validation or storage failures, and keep platform runtime qualification explicit. Android cached activation policy is unchanged. Every authenticated native request now persists a refusal fence before I/O, including attachment, notification, cleanup and sync-handshake requests. Binary keyring chunks stay within the Windows blob limit, share credential references, and use a bounded recovery journal. Both earlier protected-record formats require fresh online evidence after upgrade; downgrades require OS credential-manager cleanup. The desktop TLS refusal test fixture now carries a fixed non-secret password because macOS refuses empty-password PKCS#12 imports; test-only, no runtime or documented behavior change.

authentication.note: Upgrade Better Auth and passkey together to 1.7.12. Google keeps its callback URI, PKCE and pending native consent return URL. OAuth callbacks now preserve APIError codes, so remove the message-as-code workaround and retain readable error descriptions. Document the required additive JWT key migration; account schema, credential formats, registration policies and trusted origins are unchanged.

compatibility.note: Better Auth 1.7 requires nullable jwks.alg and jwks.crv columns. The additive migration retains encrypted Ed25519 keys and the existing restricted runtime-role grants; account and client credential formats are unchanged. Document upgrade, backup, rollback and client guidance. Align Zero at 1.11.1 and re-port durable close and outage retry. Healthy server replicas migrate incrementally; 1.9 clients start a new local database and lose unsent mutations unless drained first.
compatibility.upgrade: Stop app replicas and Zero, back up the matching recovery set, and run the additive better_auth_jwks migration as the migration owner before starting the new app and Zero. Preserve NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS runtime credentials. Drain all browser and native queues before replacing 1.9 clients. Start the updated Zero server before 1.11 clients; retain publications and slots and verify migrated replica catch-up.
compatibility.backup: Keep coordinated database and attachment backups with the original authentication secret and encryption keys. Existing encrypted keys are preserved without conversion. Retain the Zero replica snapshot and both legacy and V5 backup formats through the rollback window; test V5 restores.
compatibility.rollback: The previous app with Better Auth 1.6.23 tolerates and ignores the added nullable columns. Leave them in place during application rollback; restore older database snapshots only with matching secrets and attachments, accounting for newer data loss. Drain 1.11 client queues and downgrade clients before the server. Prefer a fresh disposable old cache over reusing migrated SQLite files. A 1.9 server cannot read V5 backup paths and resyncs; preserve current authoritative PostgreSQL.
compatibility.clientVersions: Better Auth sessions and native consent remain compatible; reload TOTP callers as described in the guide. Zero 1.11 clients require a 1.11 server. The 1.9-to-1.11 client upgrade discards its old local database, so every client must sync pending edits before updating. Keep offline clients on the old bundle until drained; never clear their storage or uninstall them.

clients.note: Document the retained runtime notice manifest, exact source URLs and SHA-256 checksums, extracted-archive integrity qualification, and unchanged incomplete runtime license coverage and binary publication block.
